source.title: Debt Without Chains
source.summary: Sukuk, qard hasan, and reimagining what debt could look like in the 21st century.
source.author: Islamic Economics
source.body_text: What if debt didn't have to be a trap? Qard hasan, the beautiful loan, is lending with no expectation of return beyond the principal, considered one of the most virtuous acts in Islam. Sukuk transform debt into shared ownership of real assets. Diminishing musharakah lets homebuyers gradually purchase their house from the bank as co-owner rather than as debtor. This final episode looks at the alternatives, from microfinance experiments in Bangladesh to sovereign sukuk issued by the UK and Hong Kong, and asks whether Islamic principles can offer a way out of the global debt crisis. With worldwide debt exceeding $300 trillion, the question isn't academic. The 7th-century insight that debt should serve people rather than enslave them may be the most radical financial idea the modern world needs.

x.single_post: Worldwide debt exceeds $300 trillion. Meanwhile, qard hasan lets you borrow with no interest expected beyond returning the principal. Why did we choose the path that turns money into chains?

linkedin.post: Global debt has surpassed $300 trillion, yet alternative models exist that challenge our assumptions about lending and borrowing. Qard hasan, the "beautiful loan" in Islamic finance, expects no interest—only the return of principal. Sukuk instruments transform traditional debt into shared ownership of tangible assets. Diminishing musharakah allows homebuyers to gradually purchase their property from the bank as a partner rather than as a debtor. From microfinance experiments in Bangladesh to sovereign sukuk issued by the UK and Hong Kong, these principles are already being tested globally. The 7th-century insight that debt should serve people rather than enslave them offers a compelling framework for addressing our current debt crisis. As we grapple with unprecedented global debt levels, perhaps it's time to seriously consider financial systems designed around human flourishing rather than extraction. Listen: https://islamiceconomics.github.io/podcast.html#ep-wd-6
